items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Lawrence Welk was across town playing his squeeze box with his seven piece group

ctx.x: And this was during the great days of the Grand Terrace when they were broadcasting. Ed Fox was the name of the guy that owned the Grand Terrace where Fletcher played after Earl Hines. In fact, he had a contract on Earl

and Fletcher. Those were his two bands, and I was in Swingland, and I used to battle these guys, and Lawrence Welk was across town playing his squeeze box with his seven piece group, and he used to come on a half hour before us on WBBM. I wish I had carried his squeeze box (unintelligible) because he laughs all the way to the bank.
You bet. About what year was this?
